- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Search this repository for code related to "memo" metadata that is derived/computed from memo content. I'm looking for:
1. Where derived metadata for memos is computed (the computation site - function/file)
2. What triggers recomputation (which operations cause it)
3. What properties are extracted from the memo content

Search broadly for terms like "memo", "snippet", "excerpt", "preview", "metadata", "derived", "computed". Look in store files, service files, helper/utility files. Check for things like extracting title, snippet, preview text, word count, etc. from memo content.

Be very thorough - search across multiple naming conventions and locations.

content.text:
Here is my complete findings report:

---

## Memo Derived/Computed Metadata -- Complete Analysis

### 1. Where Derived Metadata Is Computed

There are two separate systems for computing derived metadata from memo content:

#### A. Persistent Payload (tags + properties) -- stored in DB

**Primary computation function:**
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, function `RebuildMemoPayload` (line 74)
- This calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` which does a single-pass AST walk

**Markdown extraction engine:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, method `ExtractAll` (line 268)
- This is the core extraction routine. It parses the markdown content using goldmark, walks the AST once, and collects all metadata into an `ExtractedData` struct (defined at line 22).

#### B. Snippet (computed on-the-fly at API response time -- NOT stored in DB)

**Snippet generation:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, function `getMemoContentSnippet` (line 83)
- This calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` with a max length of 64 characters
- The `GenerateSnippet` method is in `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` (line 229)

**Snippet population into API response:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, function `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` (line 76-80) -- sets `memoMessage.Snippet`

---

### 2. What Triggers Recomputation

#### Payload rebuild (tags + properties) is triggered by:

1. **CreateMemo** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 108
   - Called whenever a new memo is created (including when a comment is created via `CreateMemoComment`, which internally calls `CreateMemo`)

2. **UpdateMemo** (when `content` field is in the update mask) -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 447
   - Only triggered when the content path is included in the update mask

3. **Batch rebuild via `Runner.RunOnce`** -- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` line 27
   - Processes ALL memos in batches of 100
   - This runner exists as infrastructure but is **not wired up** in the current server startup (`server.go` does not invoke it). It can be called manually/programmatically for migration or repair purposes.

#### Snippet is computed on-the-fly (not persisted), triggered by:

4. **Every API response** that converts a memo -- via `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` line 76

5. **Memo relation conversion** (with snippet flag) -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` lines 221-252 in `batchConvertMemoRelations`

6. **Notification payloads** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` line 323 via `memoNotificationSnippet`

7. **Individual relation conversion** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` lines 154, 162

#### Mention extraction (also uses ExtractAll):

8. **`resolveMentionTargets`** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` line 32
   - Uses `ExtractAll` to find @mentions in content for notification dispatch

---

### 3. What Properties Are Extracted from Memo Content

#### Stored in `MemoPayload` (persisted to DB):

Defined in proto at `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto`:

- **`tags`** (`repeated string`) -- All `#tag` tokens found in the markdown, deduplicated, preserving original case
- **`property.has_link`** (`bool`) -- Whether the content contains any markdown links
- **`property.has_task_list`** (`bool`) -- Whether the content contains GFM task checkboxes
- **`property.has_code`** (`bool`) -- Whether the content contains code blocks (fenced, indented) or inline code spans
- **`property.has_incomplete_tasks`** (`bool`) -- Whether any task checkboxes are unchecked
- **`property.title`** (`string`) -- The text of the first H1 heading, if the very first block-level element in the document is an `# H1` heading

#### Extracted but not stored in payload:

- **`mentions`** (`[]string`) -- All `@username` tokens found in the markdown (used for notifications, extracted via `ExtractAll` in `ExtractedData.Mentions`)

#### Computed on-the-fly (not persisted):

- **`snippet`** (`string`) -- A plain-text summary of the memo content, max 64 characters, truncated at word boundary with ` ...` suffix. Strips markdown formatting, skips code blocks, preserves inline code text, collapses block elements with spaces. Defined in the API proto at `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` line 265-266 as `OUTPUT_ONLY`.

#### Also exposed in the API proto (`OUTPUT_ONLY` fields):

From `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` lines 240-266:
- `tags` (line 241)
- `property` (line 256) -- containing `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title`
- `snippet` (line 266)

---

### Key Files Summary

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` | `RebuildMemoPayload` function + batch runner |
| `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` | Core extraction engine (`ExtractAll`, `ExtractProperties`, `ExtractTags`, `GenerateSnippet`) |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` | Calls `RebuildMemoPayload` on create (line 108) and update (line 447) |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` | `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` maps stored payload to API response + generates snippet on-the-fly |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` | `getMemoContentSnippet` helper (line 83) |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` | Uses `ExtractAll` for @mention resolution |
| `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` | `MemoPayload` definition (stored schema) |
| `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` | API-level `Memo` message with `OUTPUT_ONLY` derived fields |
| `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` | `Memo` struct with `Payload *storepb.MemoPayload` field (line 51) |
| `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` | Tests for snippet generation and extraction |

h14.

The derived metadata is computed in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` (function `RebuildMemoPayload`, line 74), which delegates to `internal/markdown/markdown.go` (`ExtractAll`, line 268) for a single-pass AST walk over the memo's markdown content. A separate on-the-fly snippet is produced by `GenerateSnippet` in the same markdown package (line 229) and attached during API response conversion in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` (`convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators`, ~line 76).

**Triggers for recomputation:**
- **CreateMemo** (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108) — called on every new memo (including comments).
- **UpdateMemo** (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447) — called when the `content` field is in the update mask.
- **Batch rebuild** via `Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, line 27) — processes all memos in batches of 100 (for migration/repair).
- **Snippet** is not persisted; it is recomputed on every API response that serializes a memo.

**Extracted properties** (persisted in `MemoPayload`, defined in `proto/store/memo.proto`):
- **`tags`** — all `#tag` tokens, deduplicated.
- **`property.has_link`** — whether the content contains any markdown links.
- **`property.has_task_list`** — whether the content contains task-list checkboxes.
- **`property.has_code`** — whether the content contains code blocks or inline code.
- **`property.has_incomplete_tasks`** — whether any task checkboxes are unchecked.
- **`property.title`** — text of the first `# H1` heading if it is the very first block element.

Additionally, **`snippet`** (a plain-text preview of up to 64 characters, truncated at a word boundary with `" ..."`) is computed on-the-fly via `GenerateSnippet` and served as an `OUTPUT_ONLY` field in the API response (`proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, line 265–266).
